experiment: Tracking Experiment T2 -- Modern Default Policy Follow-up
not_independent_confirmation: CBIoU and BoTSORT at exact 2.6.0 defaults had already been evaluated on EyeCU-Tracking-Val-v1.1, and that evaluation generated the hypothesis T2 tests. The accuracy numbers here are a reproduction, not independent confirmation. What T2 genuinely establishes is reproducibility, per-match robustness, end-to-end runtime cost, and invariant preservation.

result.selection_rule_applied: HOTA gap 0.41 < 0.5, decided on end-to-end ms/frame
result.note: CBIoU wins on both branches: it has the higher COMBINED_SEQ HOTA (59.40 vs 58.99) and the lower end-to-end cost (213.97 vs 217.78 ms/frame). The tie-break was applied because the gap fell under 0.5, and it did not change the answer.

runtime_finding: BoTSORT's +110.6% tracker-side figure from the closed bake-off translated to +1.70% end-to-end, because the detector costs 212.92 ms/frame and the tracker costs single-digit milliseconds. Inferring criterion 8 from the tracker-side number would have wrongly disqualified it.
composition_validation: The composed total was checked against a genuine fused single-process legacy measurement: 214.13 ms composed vs 213.08 ms fused, +0.49%.

adapter_bug_invalidation.reason: adapter incorrectly discarded legitimate raw tracker id 0
adapter_bug_invalidation.detail: All four modern trackers in trackers==2.6.0 number identities from 0 and use -1 for unconfirmed (utils/base_tracklet.py:27). The EyeCU adapter dropped raw_id <= 0, so every modern run silently lost one whole identity. Legacy sv.ByteTrack is 1-based and was unaffected.
